The supplied units are unchanged historical base text (lines 5706-6343), so they contain no changed lines. I reviewed both against the threat model, especially T-041, the prefix-cache SSD tier, and the TB-011 App Attest and TB-002 provider wire notes.

The release prose describes a Gemma 4 reasoning-loop guard, pair-setup stop semantics and rollout/rollback notes. These are documentation claims only. Any real behavior change lives in provider source files that are not supplied. This includes the loop-exit thinking guard (DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING), cluster pair start/stop handling, and the "at most 8,192 tokens within budget" behavior. I cannot verify them here.

The base text mentions the 30-minute vs 15-minute SSD cache TTL and no-fixed-ceiling disk budget. These are historical statements and consistent with T-041. No threat-model assumption is contradicted, no new endpoint, key custody, attestation, encryption or billing path is introduced, and no secrets appear.

The remaining integration questions concern the underlying code changes cited in the changelog: #2040 (Gemma loop exit, which injects closing-thought tokens and continues generation, so it must keep the response-encryption and cancellation paths intact and be disabled with logprobs) and #2042 (stop propagation while the leading Mac downloads or loads). Those source diffs were not supplied, so they need review if present in other batches. Missing source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. No findings are reported from this documentation-only content.
